name: GDELT Project
rate_limits: The DOC API told us to limit requests to one every 5 seconds (tested). Up to 250 records per call.
history_start: Events from 1979 (GDELT 1.0), GDELT 2.0 from February 2015, GKG from April 2013. The DOC API searches a rolling 3 months.
what_it_has: Worldwide news monitoring in 65 languages: events, themes, people, places and a tone score. The DOC 2.0 API gives article lists and tone timelines; raw files and Google BigQuery hold the long history.
simple: A robot that reads news from around the world every 15 minutes and writes down what happened and whether the mood was good or bad.
license_terms: The whole database is 100 percent free and open; citation of GDELT is expected. https://www.gdeltproject.org/data.html
quality_notes: Machine coded, so noisy, with duplicate stories and mis-tagged events. Tone is a simple word count measure. Coverage of sources grows over time, which can bias trends.

relevance.reason: The only free news source with years of history and a ready made tone score.
